summary: Request: Console view for Dedicated tier + committed throughput floor + recent throughput SLO status (CS/Sales visibility)
description:
Request from CS + Sales Enablement: add a Dedicated-focused SLO surface in Redwood Console to reduce back-and-forth with SRE/Infra when customers ask "what tier am I on", "what throughput is guaranteed", and "are we meeting the guarantee".

Background / why:
- Dedicated customers are asking for throughput guarantees in writing and for ongoing visibility (esp. procurement/security-led accounts).
- Current state: tier + committed throughput floor is in internal systems (contracts/order forms / provisioning notes), but not discoverable by CS/Sales in Console; SLO compliance requires navigating internal dashboards and knowing the right deployment_id.
- This causes slow responses, inconsistent messaging, and escalations that could be avoided with self-serve internal visibility.

Requested Console capabilities (internal visibility first; customer-visible later):
1) Dedicated overview panel (per customer org):
   - Dedicated tier: Standard | Plus | Premium (or current taxonomy)
   - Region(s) / deployment(s) included in commitment
   - Committed throughput floor (canonical metric per SLO doc; show units explicitly)
   - Burst policy summary (e.g., "burst allowed" and whether metered)

2) Per deployment details (deployment view):
   - Model pinned (name + version) and context limit used for sizing (if available)
   - Current throughput vs floor (last 15m and last 1h)
   - "SLO status" for last 7 days and last 30 days (green/yellow/red) with a short explanation of measurement window and exclusions
   - Link-outs to internal dashboards (Grafana/Looker) filtered by deployment_id

3) Recent incidents / credits (if available):
   - Show last N SLO-impacting incidents for that deployment (date, duration, incident id/status page link if public)
   - If credits were issued due to throughput SLO miss, display "credit issued" + date (no $ amount required)

Users / permissions:
- CS, Support, Sales, Solutions: internal-only (behind role gate).
- Do NOT expose raw internal SLO evaluator details publicly at this stage.

Data sources (proposal):
- Tier + committed floor: control plane config / billing contract metadata (needs a single source-of-truth surfaced via API).
- Throughput + SLO status: SRE throughput SLO evaluator summaries (or timeseries + computed rollups).
- Incidents: internal incident log + mapping to deployment_id (may be v1 manual).

Out of scope (v1):
- Customer-facing public SLO portal.
- Full contract text rendering in Console.
- Automated credit computation; only surface "credit issued" if recorded.

Acceptance criteria:
- A CS/Sales user can open Console -> Customer org -> Dedicated tab and see tier + committed throughput floor without additional tooling.
- A CS user can open a deployment and see last 15m/1h throughput vs floor and a simple last-7d/30d SLO status badge.
- UI contains clear metric units + a tooltip referencing the canonical throughput SLO definition.
- Link to the internal dashboard is pre-filtered by deployment_id and region.
- Access is restricted to internal roles (or feature flag) and audited.

Operational notes:
- This request is directly tied to recurring confusion in support tickets about streaming token accounting and which throughput numbers are "official". Ensure UI references the canonical metric and uses the post-fix streaming accounting (see related PR).

Suggested owner(s):
- Console UX + Observability: Sergio Costa / Allison Grant
- SRE for SLO semantics: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Product Dedicated for tier fields: Lauren Bishop

Business priority:
- P2: Needed for upcoming Dedicated tier + throughput SLO rollout enablement; reduce escalations and improve response times to customer questions.

References:
- Design work in progress: DES-771 (Dedicated tier UI), DES-784 (Throughput SLO status widget)
- Enablement asks coming from Sales thread requesting clearer guidance on what can be promised around burst vs committed throughput.
comments: 2025-02-21 (Rachel Kim): We’re seeing repeated escalations where AEs/CS can’t answer “what’s my committed throughput floor” without pulling SRE into a dashboard deep link. This needs to be visible in Console for internal users before we expand the SLO language rollout.

2025-02-24 (Sergio Costa): Acknowledged. We can reuse panels from observability-pack PR-842 for the visualizations, but we still need an API to fetch tier + committed floor (source-of-truth). Can Product confirm where this lives today (control plane vs billing metadata)?

2025-02-24 (Lauren Bishop): Tier + committed floor is defined at order form and then mirrored into deployment config during provisioning. Current canonical field is in control plane deployment metadata. We need to confirm naming and ensure it’s populated for legacy Dedicated deployments.

2025-02-25 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure the Console badge uses the SLO evaluator summary (not raw tokens/sec) so we respect exclusions and measurement windows. Also: streaming accounting was recently fixed; only rely on metrics post PR-19422 for any computed views.

2025-02-26 (Allison Grant): We can provide a minimal “SLO status” API that returns compliance over 7d/30d with a short reason string for most-common failure modes (capacity saturation vs customer throttling vs model mismatch). Recommend keeping it internal-only until we validate customer interpretation.

2025-02-28 (Isabelle Laurent): Sales Ops request: please include an obvious “export/share” link for internal quoting context (not customer-shareable) that includes tier, region, shape, committed floor, and last-7d status. Even a copy-to-clipboard text block would help.

2025-03-03 (Sergio Costa): Proposed v1 UI: Dedicated tab on org page + a compact widget on deployment page. Feature flag: console.dedicated_slo_internal_view. Need backend endpoint for tier fields + SLO summary; tracking in eng board separately.

2025-03-06 (Rachel Kim): Confirmed CS leadership is OK with v1 being internal-only. Main goal is faster, consistent answers during procurement/security calls. Please prioritize tooltip wording so it matches the customer-facing SLO language once finalized.
